- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price drop > 2% from 30d avg.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 3–7 day horizon.  
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3 days, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion rule: forecast = 30d avg ± 1.5×std dev for next 5 days.  
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33–1.00), model tends to overfit short-term trends; smooth forecast by 1–2% per day for 7–14 day horizon.
